chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man makes a solemn oath (ila') from his wife, and the solemn oath is that he says, 'By Allah, I will not have sexual intercourse with you, such and such [a period],' and he says, 'By Allah, I shall constrict you [in anger],' then he angers her, then he awaits her for four months. So if he returns (fa'a), and the return is that he reconciles with his family or divorces her at that time, and a divorce does not take place between the two of them until he pauses, even if it is after the four months, until he either returns or divorces.

key_terms.إِيفَاءُ: The fulfillment/return (in the context of Ila')
key_terms.إِيلَاءُ: Solemn oath of abstention from sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and procedure for Ila' (solemn oath of abstention) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the Shia jurisprudence of 'Ila'', where a husband's solemn oath to abstain from intercourse triggers a four-month waiting period (Ihtibat) before the separation becomes final. It emphasizes that reconciliation or divorce must occur within this timeframe to avoid indefinite limbo, reflecting the Quranic principle of giving the spouse time to decide. The narration clarifies that the divorce is not immediate but contingent upon the expiration of the period without reconciliation.
